text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No GenAI or personal data review recorded","detail":"The proposal deploys a generative AI LLM and identifies customers by phone number (personal data), but records no AI/legal/privacy/security review. Only vendor selection is mentioned as in progress.","evidence_quote":"Deploy a GenAI chatbot using an LLM that identifies the customer by phone number and answers order status questions from order history.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Complete and record GenAI governance, privacy/data protection, and security reviews (including vendor data handling) before launch."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Deflection claim lacks source","detail":"The 60% contact deflection is stated as an expectation without any source, pilot data, or benchmark.","evidence_quote":"We expect the chatbot to deflect 60% of contacts.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite supporting data (pilot, vendor benchmark, historical analysis) or reframe as a hypothesis with a justified range."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Vague success metric name","detail":"\"Customer happiness\" is not a canonical glossary metric; it is ambiguous (CSAT, NPS, etc.) and its measurement is unclear. It also does not align with the deflection goal.","evidence_quote":"Customer happiness: from 4.0 to 4.4 within 12 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use a defined glossary metric (e.g., Contact Rate, Support CSAT, or deflection/containment rate) with a clear definition."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for chatbot accuracy and escalation","detail":"A customer-facing LLM answering order questions needs guardrails such as answer accuracy/hallucination rate, escalation/handoff failure, and resolution quality (e.g., repeat contact rate). Only Contact Rate and Delivery CSAT are listed, and Delivery CSAT does not measure the chatbot interaction.","evidence_quote":"Contact Rate: stop if it rises by more than 1 per 100.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for incorrect answer rate, escalation/handoff success, repeat contact rate, and chatbot-specific CSAT."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days standard and mismatched with metric horizon","detail":"The plan runs 3 weeks, which meets the 14-day minimum, but the success metric targets a 12-week horizon, so the test cannot measure it. The MDE is also defined for contacts per 100, which is not the stated primary success metric (customer happiness), so power does not apply to the primary metric.","evidence_quote":"Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.5 contacts per 100, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align the primary metric, MDE, power, and duration; compute MDE/power for the actual success metric and run long enough to observe it."}]}
